title: Revolutions That Made the Modern World: American, French, and Russian

questions.question: Which Enlightenment thinker argued for the separation of powers into legislative, executive, and judicial branches?
questions.rationale: Montesquieu's The Spirit of the Laws argued for separating the three powers — the architectural principle of the 1787 American Constitution.

questions.question: The American Declaration of Independence was adopted on:
questions.rationale: Jefferson's Declaration was adopted on 4 July 1776; the Constitution followed in 1787 and the Bill of Rights in 1791.

questions.question: The American war ended decisively when Cornwallis surrendered at:
questions.rationale: Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown in 1781; the Treaty of Paris (1783) then recognised the United States.

questions.question: On 17 June 1789, the Third Estate proclaimed itself:
questions.rationale: The Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly, sealing the claim with the Tennis Court Oath of 20 June — no dissolution until France had a constitution.

questions.question: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen was adopted in:
questions.rationale: The Declaration of 26 August 1789 proclaimed liberty, property, and equality before the law — the French Revolution's manifesto.

questions.question: The Reign of Terror (1793-94) is associated with:
questions.rationale: The Jacobins under Robespierre ruled through the Committee of Public Safety, sending some 17,000 people to the guillotine before Robespierre himself fell in Thermidor (July 1794).

questions.question: Lenin called the revolution of 1905 the 'dress rehearsal' for 1917. The event that triggered it was:
options: Bloody Sunday, when troops fired on Father Gapon's petitioners
questions.rationale: On Bloody Sunday (January 1905) troops fired on peaceful petitioners outside the Winter Palace, sparking strikes, the Potemkin mutiny, and the Duma concession.

questions.question: In the February Revolution of 1917:
options: The Bolsheviks seized the Winter Palace
Tsar Nicholas II abdicated and a Provisional Government took over
Lenin returned in a sealed train
The Red Army won the civil war
questions.rationale: Bread riots and mutinies at Petrograd forced Nicholas II's abdication; the Provisional Government (Lvov, then Kerensky) continued the unpopular war.

questions.question: The October Revolution of 7-8 November 1917 was carried out by:
options: The Bolsheviks under Lenin and Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee
questions.rationale: Lenin's Bolsheviks, organised by Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee, seized key points in Petrograd; the cruiser Aurora's shot signalled the Winter Palace assault.

questions.question: Stalin's first Five-Year Plan (1928) was paired with:
questions.rationale: From 1928 Stalin forced heavy industrialisation through Five-Year Plans and collectivised farms — dekulakisation and the 1932-33 famine (Holodomor) followed.
